protocol.selection_order: All scope exclusions by registry_order, then all exceptions by counselor_programme_id; resume by audit_population plus counselor_programme_id.
protocol.population_start: Current normalized data/registry/programmes.csv; upstream DUO/RIO population is out of scope.
protocol.confirmed_meaning: Supports only the facts and decision within audit_scope. For no-defensible-ucr-match, confirmation applies only to external-programme basis; UCR reassessment remains pending.
protocol.outdated_rule: Requires dated evidence establishing that the original decision was supportable and that a later change superseded it. Record temporal uncertainty explicitly when historical evidence cannot distinguish incorrect from outdated.
protocol.resolved_external_curriculum_action: Normally reassess-exception: an externally reconstructable comparator alone does not establish UCR feasibility.
protocol.reprocess_as_comparison_rule: Recommend only when comparison eligibility is independently established; do not infer it merely from resolved external evidence.
protocol.incomplete_batches: Keep pending cases explicit without audit_finding; never count pending cases as audited.
protocol.final_reconciliation: Every excluded target and every current exception must have exactly one completed audit entry per audit_population; report missing in-scope records separately.

reconciliation_evidence.exception_type_check: Read all 140 exception canonical JSON records directly; verified their IDs and recordStatus and inventoried exception.type only. This is population enumeration, not exception research.
reconciliation_evidence.comparison_count_basis: Current generated review index, with its complete ID set reconciled to both registry scope and canonical filenames; comparison contents were not audited.

cases.existing_substantive_exception_reason: German-language proficiency, German linguistics and literature, German-speaking-country immersion and Dutch–German cultural exchange form the core of this bachelor. UCR currently offers no German-language course or specialist German-studies sequence. Related courses in general literature, history, communication and European politics cannot form a credible 24-course closest-match programme without treating them as substitutes for missing German-language study.
cases.audit_scope: External-programme identity, compulsory German-studies core, immersion and published source context only; no independent UCR feasibility judgment.
cases.audit_basis: Current official pages support the defining German-language, linguistics, literature/culture, Dutch–German exchange and compulsory immersion basis. Confirmation applies to that external core only. The stored first/second-year labels (2026–2027) differ from the currently published indicative 2027–2028/2028–2029 pages. The current year-two page describes 30 EC free space with broader options, whereas component y2-minors restricts it to two Humanities minors. These source-context details need reassessment even though the external core is confirmed.
cases.recommended_fix: In a later authorized production task, determine the applicable academic/cohort year from the official education catalogue or programme regulations; refresh comparator.academicYear, sourceNotes, changed course labels and y2-minors. Describe 30 EC as free space if the applicable curriculum supports that. Retain the supported German core, preserve the indicative future-year caveat, and assess UCR feasibility independently in stage two. This audit does not edit the canonical exception.
cases.unresolved_factual_question: The currently published pages address a prospective 2027-entry sequence. Which formal curriculum and second-year elective restrictions apply to the intended Fall 2026 cohort? Historical page evidence was not established, so the observed source-context discrepancies do not distinguish an original error from a later change.
cases.ucr_side_assessment_note: The existing UCR claim is reproduced as provenance only. Neither its course evidence nor the no-defensible-match conclusion was independently validated in this stage.
cases.governing_rule: First-stage no-defensible-ucr-match external-basis-only scope; Production Instructions §4.4.

provenance.existing_comparator_source_notes: Radboud presents 60 EC in each of three years. Year 1 contains twelve compulsory 5-EC courses; its two 0-EC academic support activities do not count toward the 180 EC. Year 2 contains three 5-EC required courses, a 15-EC German-speaking-country stay within the major, and 30 EC of minor space. Year 3 contains four 5-EC required courses, a 10-EC independent bachelor thesis/tutorial, and 30 EC of restricted minor space (two Humanities minors or the educational minor). The educational minor is an optional route, not a required qualification. Prospectus year pages are indicative and do not establish a guaranteed 2028–2029 year-three timetable for a Fall 2026 entrant.

It contains general literature, linguistics via Psycholinguistics, history, communication and European politics, but no German-language course, German-specific literature or linguistics sequence, or German-speaking-country immersion. Those related courses cannot support a defensible 24-course closest match.

Two 0-EC academic support activities are excluded from the 180-EC total. In year two, six required 5-EC courses total 30 EC, with 30 EC of restricted Faculty of Arts minor choices (two 15-EC minors); additional English language/culture minors are optional rather than required. These are meaningful adjacent studies, but the workbook has no sequence in English phonetics, phonology, syntax, historical English, English language proficiency or period-specific British and American literature. The nearest courses cannot sustain a defensible 24-course English Language and Culture closest match.

cases.existing_substantive_exception_reason: The Radboud degree is an integrated molecular biology AND chemistry programme. Its compulsory first year already includes atoms and molecules, analytical chemistry and a chemical-analysis lab, organic chemistry and synthesis lab, biochemistry and its lab, thermodynamics, cell biophysics and a molecular-sciences lab. The later compulsory core deepens organic, inorganic and analytical chemistry, crystal structure, biomolecular mechanisms and structural bioinformatics, then requires a supervised 12-EC research internship. UCR offers valuable molecular-cell and biomedical courses but lacks a sequence in organic/inorganic/analytical/physical chemistry, molecular spectroscopy and synthesis, and has only one broad life-science laboratory course. A 24-course UCR schedule could sustain biomedical biology with data methods, but it would omit the defining chemistry and multi-lab spine and would misrepresent equivalence to this molecular-science degree.

cases.existing_substantive_exception_reason: Radboud Natural Sciences teaches physics, chemistry, (molecular) biology and mathematics together. A 24-course environmental/biomedical/data curriculum would be a different degree, not a faithful closest response to this exact target.

cases.existing_substantive_exception_reason: PWPO is an integrated academic primary-teacher-education degree that confers primary-school teaching qualification. The core includes 33 EC in four supervised classroom placements, direct instruction, classroom management and pedagogical practice, plus sustained subject didactics in early reading, handwriting, spelling, speaking and writing, reading comprehension and literature, mathematics, world orientation, art and multilingual learning. A coherent 24-course developmental-psychology programme could respond to some child-development interests, but would omit the defining teaching practice and profession-specific academic preparation of this named degree. It cannot be presented as its closest defensible UCR response.

VU's current official overview page (s0, checked 2026-09-27) confirms a 180-EC, three-year bachelor offered '3 jaar Voltijd en deeltijd' with three co-equal afstudeerrichtingen chosen from year 1: Christelijke theologie (Theologie), Islamitische theologie (Islam, which s0 itself describes as 'the only Islamic-theological WO bachelor in the Netherlands'), and Religie en Levensbeschouwing (also branded 'Zingeving, geestelijke verzorging en samenleving'); s4, a third-party study-choice aggregator republishing VU's own submitted programme data, independently confirms the 180-ECTS total and the same three afstudeerrichtingen. Applying the Section 2.1 neutral route-selection hierarchy (the target is generic and no route is clearly more representative): the Theologie track's own current page (s2) requires a compulsory Hebrew (Hebreeuws I-III) and Greek (Greek I-III + New Testament) biblical-language sequence and offers tradition-specific confessional seminary sub-tracks (Hersteld Hervormd, Baptist, Mennonite); the Islam track requires compulsory Arabic-language study and Qur'an/hadith/fiqh confessional training (s0; independently corroborated by generator-eligible programme-interest rows 5410, 5411, 5412, 5413 naming Qur'an/hadith exegesis, Sharia jurisprudence and Arabic-language study as structural Islam-track content). Religie en Levensbeschouwing is instead described by its own current page (s1) as an explicitly comparative, multireligious, 'dialogisch' course of study engaging several religious traditions rather than forming students within one confessional tradition, with no compulsory classical/liturgical-language sequence. It is therefore the least specialized/most general of the three formal routes and is selected as the reconstructed route. However, s0, s1 and s2 give only qualitative year-by-year course-name lists for their respective tracks (for the selected route: year 1 covers the origin of religious traditions and world religions plus 'Conflict and Peacebuilding'; year 2 covers 'Zingeving, religie en mentale gezondheid' and 'Religie en trauma'; year 3 includes a flexible-location minor, 'Scriptieseminar en bachelorscriptie', and electives such as 'Godsdienstfilosofie') without any EC weight, compulsory-versus-elective status, or credit table for a single component. VU's own current regulations page (s3, checked 2026-09-27) states that the formal Teaching and Examination Regulations for every VU programme are 'published in the Study Guide' at studiegids.vu.nl; that portal's landing page carries only top-level dynamic category navigation with no extractable curriculum content, and a constructed direct URL for this exact study guide entry returned HTTP 404 to available retrieval tools, matching the same dynamic-portal limitation already documented for another current VU counselor target (cp-000118). Reasonable further search located only one standalone official OER PDF for a VU theology bachelor, 'Onderwijs- en Examenregeling Bacheloropleiding Theologie 2017-2018' (s5); its own text shows 'Minor Islam' offered only as one elective minor within a single undifferentiated Theologie bachelor, not as one of three co-equal afstudeerrichtingen chosen from year 1, so it predates and does not reliably describe the current three-route structure and is preserved only as evidence of how substantially the formal structure has since changed, not used to supply component credits. No third-party source (s4; the Qompas study-choice listing checked during research) publishes a per-course EC table either. Because no accessible current or formally adopted source establishes exact EC weights, compulsory/elective status or a stable component list for the selected route, no 180-EC component list is supplied.

cases.existing_substantive_exception_reason: The defining curriculum of the selected route is a chemical-engineering sequence built on physics and chemistry: Fundamentals of Engineering, Chemistry and Chemical Engineering, and Thermodynamics and Engineering Physics in the compulsory first year, physics, electronics, chemistry and biology laboratory skills, fluid mechanics and heat and mass transfer in year 2, and in year 3 chemical engineering thermodynamics and kinetics, separation processes, reactor engineering, chemical plant design, process design and control, unit-operations and industrial-process-design skills and a 25-EC engineering thesis. UCR offers circular-economy, life-cycle, energy and environmental-engineering-adjacent courses, a mathematics and numerical-methods line and biochemistry and cell-biology courses, but no physics, chemistry sequence, thermodynamics, transport phenomena, reactor or process engineering, mechanics or engineering design. A 24-course programme would be a sustainability-and-mathematics programme with a small circular-economy core padded with unrelated life-science or computing courses, and it would not reproduce the programme's engineering substance; the unmatched components include essentially all of the 25-EC concentration course sequence, the engineering physics and chemistry core and the thesis. The comparison would have to present adjacent sustainability courses as substitutes for engineering content that UCR does not teach.

provenance.existing_comparator_academic_year: 2026-2027 (Education and Examination Regulations BSc Circular Engineering, Faculty of Science and Engineering, in force 1 September 2026; programme pages checked 2026-10-03)
provenance.existing_comparator_source_notes: The programme pages (s1, s2) describe the structure in words only: a common first year, a second year of electives, skills and projects, and a third year with one of four concentrations and a thesis; they give no course list with EC. The 180-EC reconstruction therefore uses the 2026-2027 Education and Examination Regulations (s0): Article 3.6 (study load per year), 3.7 (core), 3.8 (electives), 3.9 (concentration and thesis) and Appendix I (course overview). Year 1: eight mandatory 5-EC courses, 10 EC of skills courses and two 5-EC projects. Year 2: eight elective 5-EC courses and four elective 2.5-EC skills courses (two courses and one skill per period, chosen from the published framework) plus two mandatory 5-EC projects; the framework is availability-dependent, so one coherent valid selection linked to the Circular Chemical Engineering concentration is instantiated (Organic Chemistry, Fluid Mechanics, Numerical Methods, Polymeric Materials, Differential Equations, Biochemistry, Heat & Mass Transfer, Remake Reuse Repair Recycle; skills in organic chemistry, statistics, fabrication and design, and analytical and physical chemistry) and is flagged here as an instantiation of restricted choice rather than a fixed requirement. The Heat & Mass Transfer elective is explicitly linked to this concentration, which satisfies the requirement that one elective be linked to a third-year concentration. Year 3: one mandatory 5-EC core course (Ethical and Philosophical Reflections), the Circular Chemical Engineering concentration of five 5-EC courses (the fifth, Circular Process Design and Control, shown in the period 3-4 slot) and two 2.5-EC skills courses, and the 25-EC bachelor thesis (BTH3010). Totals are 60 EC per year and 180 EC overall.
provenance.existing_ucr_course_evidence: Reviewed all 151 course rows in the current enriched UCR workbook, including descriptions, outline-derived profiles, topics, prerequisites and planned terms. Relevant adjacent offerings are ENSSUST112 Life Cycle Analysis & Circular Economy (life-cycle assessment and circularity), ENSDELT311 R3: Recycling, Recovery, Remediation (circular-economy strategies with laboratory skills and inorganic chemistry), ENSSUST211 Energy & Sustainability and ENSSUST311 Renewable System Design (energy systems and technical-economic assessment), ENSDELT111 Building with Nature, DISGATE102 Mathematical Methods, DISMATH211 Linear Algebra, DISMATH214 Advanced Calculus (multivariable calculus and differential equations), DISMATH213 Computational & Numerical Methods, DISMATH312 Linear Systems, DISDATA312 Robotics, HCBGATE101 Foundation of Life, Health & Biomedicine, HCBLIFE211 Molecular Cell Biology, HCBLIFE213 Biochemistry and HCBLIFE214 Life Science Laboratory. They give partial counterparts to Engineering in a Circular Economy, the Life Cycle Assessment Project, Calculus, Linear Algebra, Multivariate Calculus, Numerical Methods, Differential Equations, Biochemistry and Biotechnology, but none to Fundamentals of Engineering, Chemistry and Chemical Engineering, Thermodynamics and Engineering Physics, the physics, electronics and chemistry laboratory skills, Fluid Mechanics, Heat & Mass Transfer, the five-course Circular Chemical Engineering concentration with its skills courses, the design projects or the thesis. No course in the workbook covers physics, thermodynamics, chemical or process engineering, reactor or separation technology, or mechanics, so these isolated adjacent offerings cannot support a coherent 24-course Circular Engineering programme.

cases.existing_substantive_exception_reason: The programme's defining academic identity is sustained Protestant Christian theology and theology-specific method: systematic, historical, practical and biblical theology; Greek and Hebrew; exegesis in the source languages; theology, aesthetics and culture; Reformation history; Judaism and Islam in theological context; personal worldview formation; and a 15-EC final theological project. Only the 30-EC minor is broadly open. UCR offers adjacent philosophy, ethics, history, sociology, politics, literature, art history and cultural analysis, but no sustained theology, scripture, source-language, exegesis or pastoral curriculum. A 24-course UCR schedule assembled from neighbouring humanities and social sciences would erase the target's defining theological sequence and would not be a defensible substantive match.

provenance.existing_curriculum_context: The formally published 2026-2027 Groningen curriculum totals exactly 180 ECTS: 60 ECTS in each of three years, with no tracks, minor space or electives. Its 29 compulsory components progress from healthy-human and healthy-mouth science, prevention and simulated professional skills through compromised oral health, oral diseases and further clinical skills to dental radiation protection, diagnosis and restoration, advanced professional skills and a 12-ECTS supervised Bachelor Clinic. The OER makes the skills sequence prerequisite-dependent and requires completion of both second-year professional-skills components, oral healthcare in context and most second-year theoretical components before entry to the Bachelor Clinic.
provenance.existing_comparator_source_notes: The University of Groningen's current Dentistry documents page publishes the linked 2026-2027 Education and Examination Regulations (OER) as the governing bachelor regulation. Although the PDF's browser metadata title is 'concept', its running header identifies it throughout as the 2026-2027 Dentistry bachelor OER; the official documents page presents it as the current OER. Articles 3.6, 4.1 and 7.1 establish an ordinary three-year, 180-ECTS curriculum of 60 ECTS per year. All 29 listed components are compulsory and total 60+60+60=180 ECTS. Article 7.1 explicitly confirms that there are no tracks, no minor space and no electives, so the normalized generic Dentistry target has no route to select. The current programme page independently confirms a 36-month, 180-ECTS, Dutch-taught bachelor that integrates biomedical, behavioural and dental science with extensive technical-skills training and patient care. Practical procedures are first trained on artificial jaws and teeth; diagnosis and treatment begin in Years 2 and 3; the curriculum culminates in the Bachelor Clinic and scientific work.

provenance.existing_comparator_source_notes: TU Delft's official programme and student portal, checked 2026-09-29, describe the current broad Dutch-language Bachelor Bouwkunde / Architecture, Urbanism and Building Sciences and link the 2026-2027 study guide. TU Delft's published bachelor outcomes integrate architecture, urbanism, landscape architecture, building technology, management of the built environment and geo-information; they require design across scales, the relationship between people and the physical environment, sustainability, building life cycles, reuse and the synthesis of technology, design and society. The current student portal separately identifies the Bachelor 5 minor. provenance.existing_ucr_course_evidence: Reviewed all 151 current enriched UCR workbook rows, including names, descriptions, outline-derived profiles, disciplines, topics, methods, prerequisites and planned Fall 2026 cohort terms. ENSDELT111 Building with Nature provides one ecosystem-based engineering/design course; ENSSUST315 Spatial Planning and ENSENVI211 Earth Observation provide spatial engineering, GIS, remote sensing and geospatial analysis; BENENTR111 Consumer Product Design teaches a product-development studio; ENSGATE101, ENSSUST112 and ENSSUST311 provide broad materials, life-cycle/circular-economy and renewable-system content; MCCHEAM112, MCCHEAM212 and MCCHEAM315 address archaeology, heritage and some architectural history. cases.existing_substantive_exception_reason: Life Science and Technology is an integrated biotechnology and bioprocess-engineering degree. Its compulsory spine combines molecular and cellular biology with bio-organic and chemical biology, molecular analytical methods, thermodynamics and transport phenomena, microbial physiology and biotechnology, genetic engineering, biocatalysis, bioinformatics, bioprocess modelling, basic biotechnology techniques, a microbial-biotechnology practicum, sustainable process design and a 20-EC final project. UCR offers meaningful molecular biology, biochemistry, immunology, genetics, pharmacology, laboratory, calculus, programming and data-science courses. It does not offer the required chemistry and bioprocess-engineering progression, including bio-organic and chemical biology, bioprocess thermodynamics, transport phenomena, microbial process engineering, biocatalysis, reactor/process modelling and sustainable biotechnological process design, nor an equivalent advanced biotechnology laboratory and capstone sequence. Combining UCR's strongest life-science, mathematics and computational courses would create a substantial molecular-biomedicine pathway, but not a defensible Life Science and Technology comparator.

HCBGATE101 Foundation of Life, Health and Biomedicine, HCBLIFE211 Molecular Cell Biology, HCBLIFE213 Biochemistry, HCBLIFE311 Molecular Pathology and Genetics, HCBBIOM313 Mechanisms of Disease and HCBCOGN112 Neurobiology provide relevant biological foundations. HCBLIFE214 Life Science Laboratory introduces biochemical and molecular laboratory work involving blood, proteins, bacteria, DNA and bioinformatics. UCR's mathematics and computing courses are useful supporting work, but without the compulsory physics, nanoscale measurement and integrated experimental progression the target programme's defining quantitative-biophysical formation is absent. UCR also lacks TU/e's staged applied-physics challenge and laboratory work, advanced experimental research course and discipline-specific Bachelor Final Project. The closest possible 24-course UCR combination would therefore be a mathematical and sustainability-oriented liberal-arts pathway with the target programme's defining physical theory, experimentation and engineering formation absent.

cases.existing_substantive_exception_reason: Leiden Bio-Pharmaceutical Sciences is an integrated experimental drug-science degree. Its compulsory spine combines general and organic chemistry, molecular and cell biology, biochemistry, physiology, genetics, pharmacology, pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics, ADME, toxicology, bio-analysis, drug design and synthesis, biopharmacy and biophysics, multiple discipline-specific laboratories, modern drug development, a 30-EC specialisation and a 16-EC bachelor research project. The selected broad route adds pharmaceutical formulation and analysis, technology, quality and pharmacotherapy. UCR offers a strong molecular-biomedical cluster, one pharmacology course, quantitative and data-science methods, and one life-science laboratory, but no chemistry sequence, medicinal or pharmaceutical chemistry, pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics, drug-design and synthesis sequence, pharmaceutical analysis, formulation science, pharmaceutical technology and quality, staged drug-science laboratories or comparable bio-pharmaceutical research capstone. A 24-course UCR programme would therefore become general biomedical science rather than a defensible Bio-Pharmaceutical Sciences comparator.

cases.existing_substantive_exception_reason: Leiden Chinese Studies is an integrated area-studies and language degree. Its defining core contains a cumulative modern Mandarin sequence, classical Chinese, Chinese-language source work, Chinese history and culture across premodern and modern periods, contemporary Chinese politics, economics and society, region-specific disciplinary choices, an intensive study period in China or Taiwan and an independent Chinese Studies paper. UCR offers strong general courses in history, politics, international relations, sociology, economics, literature, media, philosophy and cultural heritage, but it offers no Mandarin or classical Chinese language sequence, no Chinese-language source training, no China- or East-Asia-focused course sequence and no comparable situated study or Chinese Studies research environment. A 24-course UCR programme would therefore replace the programme's defining language-and-area formation with adjacent general disciplines rather than constitute a defensible Chinese Studies comparison.

provenance.existing_curriculum_context: The live 2026-2027 Leiden curriculum accounts for exactly 180 EC across three 60-EC years. The represented pathway preserves 55 EC of Year 1 compulsory work plus one 5-EC bound elective; 25 EC of Year 2 compulsory work, 15 EC of selected China-focused content, one 5-EC shared East Asia course and one 15-EC Mandarin 2c option; and 10 EC of compulsory third-year Mandarin, one 5-EC language option, one 5-EC content option, a 10-EC BA paper and 30 EC of open elective space. There is no formal route. The restricted choices instantiate one coherent political-economy-and-society emphasis without changing the programme's broad identity.
provenance.existing_comparator_source_notes: The live Leiden Study Guide product identifies a current 180-EC Chinese Studies bachelor with three 60-EC years and no formal graduation routes. The coherent pathway represented here combines every compulsory component with a political-economy-and-society emphasis in the restricted choices. Year 1 contains 55 EC of compulsory Mandarin, classical Chinese, Chinese history, contemporary China, Chinese culture and digital-humanities study plus the 5-EC Classics of Asia bound elective. Year 2 contains 25 EC of compulsory language, contemporary-China and philosophy-of-science study, 15 EC of selected China-focused content, one 5-EC shared East Asia course and the 15-EC Mandarin 2c study period in China or Taiwan. Year 3 contains 10 EC of compulsory Mandarin, one 5-EC Chinese-language choice, one 5-EC China-focused content choice, a 10-EC BA paper and 30 EC of genuine elective space. The selected content choices form one valid political-economy-and-society pathway; they are not a formal route and were selected independently of UCR fit. The zero-credit first-year mentoring component is noted in the official product but omitted from the positive-credit component list.
provenance.existing_ucr_course_evidence: Reviewed all 151 records in the current GitHub main data/reference/ucr_courses_enriched.xlsx (SHA-256 7bf6c2ae9de0837086ec741c27bd94ed7e85dff2d25bde619ecd50cc4d685879), including names, descriptions, outline-derived profiles, disciplines, topics, methods, prerequisites and planned availability. GOSHIST111 Modern History, GOSHIST211 History of Empires and GOSHIST312 History Research Seminar provide historical frameworks and research practice; GOSPOLI112 Foundations of Comparative Politics, GOSPOLI212 Theory of International Relations, BENECON111 Introduction to Economics, BENECON211 International Macroeconomics, BENENTR312 International Business & Governance, GOSSOCI111 Introduction to Sociology, GOSSOCI214 Modern Sociology and GOSSOCI212 Qualitative Research Methodology support political, economic and social analysis; MCCLITR111 Introduction to Literary Studies, MCCLITR211 World Myth & Literature, MCCMEDI111 Introduction to Film & Media, MCCMEDI311 Media & Race, MCCHEAM111 Introduction to Western Art History and GOSPHIL111 Introduction to Western Philosophy provide general cultural, literary, media, heritage and philosophical study. These are transferable disciplinary perspectives, not China-specific courses. The workbook contains no Mandarin course, classical Chinese, Chinese linguistics, Chinese history, Chinese literature, Chinese philosophy or religion, Chinese politics or economy, East Asian regional studies, Chinese-language primary-source training, China/Taiwan study component or Chinese Studies research capstone. It therefore cannot support an academically honest 24-course closest match.

cases.existing_substantive_exception_reason: Leiden is phasing in a revised Criminology curriculum. The current 2026-2027 Study Guide establishes the revised first and second years, but it expressly labels the displayed third year as the old curriculum for students who began in 2024 or earlier and states that Year 3 of the revised curriculum will only be published in the 2027-2028 guide. Combining the 120 EC revised sequence with the 60 EC legacy third year would create a pathway that no Fall 2026 entrant can follow. The missing applicable third-year structure cannot be inferred from the outgoing curriculum without inventing compulsory, elective, research and thesis requirements.

cases.audit_basis: The stored revised first/second years are supported at 60 + 60 EC, with twelve required 5-EC modules each. The current guide explicitly restricts its displayed third year to entrants in 2024 or earlier; the revised third year will appear in the 2027–2028 guide. No complete revised-cohort 180-EC pathway is established.
cases.recommended_fix: Preserve the verified 120-EC subset, zero-credit formation notes and active Dutch target. Refresh sources only when applicable revised year 3 is published; do not append the outgoing third year.

provenance.existing_curriculum_context: The applicable revised curriculum is supported for 120 EC: 60 EC in Year 1 and 60 EC in Year 2, each composed of twelve compulsory 5-EC modules. It establishes integrated criminological theory, legal and criminal-justice study, psychological and sociological explanations, qualitative and quantitative methods, professional skills, policy evaluation, victims and offenders, cybercrime, investigation and prosecution, forensic psychology and experimental methods. The current product confirms that the programme as a whole is 180 EC, but the remaining revised 60 EC are not yet published. cases.existing_substantive_exception_reason: Leiden Tax Law is a cumulative Dutch legal degree with a specialist fiscal spine. Its compulsory curriculum combines the foundations of constitutional, private, criminal, international, European, administrative, Roman, obligations and company law with income taxation, value added and real-estate transfer taxation, corporation tax, international tax law, procedural and formal tax law, financial accounting, public-sector economics, tax ethics, fiscal advocacy and a Tax Law thesis. UCR offers a useful six-course law-and-justice sequence plus economics, public economics, accounting and business-law courses, but no dedicated tax-law course or progression in income, corporate, indirect, international, procedural and formal taxation. A 24-course UCR pathway could examine law, markets and public policy broadly, but it could not preserve the target's academic identity as Tax Law.

Current revised first two years each verify 60 EC.

provenance.existing_curriculum_context: The current 2026-2027 curriculum accounts for the full 180 EC: 60 EC of first-year legal foundations, 60 EC of second-year legal and fiscal study, and a third year comprising 40 EC of compulsory advanced fiscal study, 15 EC of genuine elective space and a 5-EC Tax Law thesis. Across years 2 and 3 the required specialist courses form a connected progression through individual income taxation, indirect taxation, financial accounting, public-sector economics and tax ethics into procedural and formal tax law, international taxation, corporation tax and fiscal moot-court practice. The programme therefore cannot be represented by a few isolated courses about taxation or public policy.
provenance.existing_comparator_academic_year: 2026-2027 curriculum checked 2026-10-06
provenance.existing_comparator_source_notes: The live Leiden Study Guide identifies a three-year, 180-EC Tax Law bachelor. The first year establishes a broad Dutch-law foundation and introduces tax law and legal methods. The second year combines private, criminal, European and company law with individual income taxation, value added and real-estate transfer taxation, financial accounting, public-sector economics and the ethics of taxation. The third year requires tax-law moot court, procedural and formal tax law, public-sector economics, tax ethics, international tax law, corporation tax and a bachelor thesis, while preserving 15 EC of genuine elective space. No formal route or specialisation is required for the generic normalized target; the programme's full-time curriculum supplies the academically neutral content reconstruction for the registered full-time and part-time modes.
provenance.existing_ucr_course_evidence: Reviewed all 151 records in the current GitHub main data/reference/ucr_courses_enriched.xlsx (SHA-256 7bf6c2ae9de0837086ec741c27bd94ed7e85dff2d25bde619ecd50cc4d685879), including names, descriptions, outline-derived profiles, disciplines, topics, methods, prerequisites and planned availability. GOSGATE102 Law, Society & Justice, GOSLAWJ111 Human Rights: Law & Philosophy, GOSLAWJ211 Criminal Law & Criminal Justice, GOSLAWJ212 Introduction to Public International Law, GOSLAWJ213 Comparative Constitutional Law, GOSLAWJ311 Principles of Private Law and GOSLAWJ312 Foundations of European Union Law provide meaningful broad legal formation. BENECON111 Introduction to Economics, BENECON211 International Macroeconomics, BENECON212 Microeconomics & Behavior, BENECON311 Public Economics and BENECON312 Econometrics provide economic and policy analysis; BENBUSI112 Accounting & Corporate Finance and BENBUSI311 Transnational Business Law add adjacent accounting and business-law study. Public Economics explicitly addresses taxation, public goods, externalities and government spending, but the workbook contains no dedicated tax law, individual income taxation, corporation tax, value added or transfer tax, international taxation, fiscal procedure, formal tax law, taxpayer-rights or tax-enforcement course, no Dutch administrative and obligations-law progression, and no fiscal moot court or Tax Law thesis. The closest possible UCR combination would consequently be an interdisciplinary law-and-economics pathway, not a defensible substitute for the comparator's specialist fiscal-law sequence.

cases.existing_substantive_exception_reason: Leiden French Language and Culture is a cumulative French-medium language-and-humanities degree. Its defining compulsory formation integrates sustained advanced French speaking, listening and academic writing through C1 with grammar, syntax, phonology, French linguistics, literature across historical periods, French and Francophone cultural history, programme-specific research seminars and a French-focused thesis. UCR offers strong English-medium courses in literary, communication, film, media, historical and cultural analysis plus one psycholinguistics course, but it has no taught French-language acquisition sequence and no French or Francophone studies curriculum. A 24-course UCR pathway could study literature, media, identity and postcolonial questions comparatively, but it could not preserve the target's academic identity as French Language and Culture.

provenance.existing_curriculum_context: The official curriculum accounts for the full 180 EC as 60 EC of fixed first-year French language, linguistics, literature and culture study; 80 EC of upper-year programme-specific language and humanities formation; 30 EC of genuine free-choice space; and a 10-EC BA thesis. The current cohort rules require multiple French-programme seminars, including research seminars, alongside advanced written and oral language work. Leiden's official programme material states that classes are French-medium and foregrounds the Francophone world beyond France. Even after the 30-EC free-choice block is preserved, the remaining 150 EC form a connected French-proficiency and French/Francophone-studies core rather than a collection of general humanities electives.

provenance.existing_comparator_source_notes: Leiden's latest published target-specific study guide identifies a three-year, 180-EC French Language and Culture bachelor centred on French proficiency, linguistics, literature and cultural study. The fully fixed 60-EC first year combines advanced French, oral comprehension and expression, grammar, phonology, French linguistics, literary studies across periods and French cultural history. The upper years continue written and oral French to C1, syntax, Francophone literatures and societies, modern literature, poetry and theatre, research methodology, programme seminars and a 10-EC thesis, while preserving 30 EC of genuine free-choice space. The official programme brochure confirms that teaching is conducted in French and that the programme develops specialist knowledge of French language, literature and culture in France and the wider Francophone world. No formal route or specialisation is required for the generic normalized target; alternating seminars are represented as programme seminar space rather than filled with an invented choice.
provenance.existing_ucr_course_evidence: Reviewed all 151 records in the current GitHub main data/reference/ucr_courses_enriched.xlsx (SHA-256 7bf6c2ae9de0837086ec741c27bd94ed7e85dff2d25bde619ecd50cc4d685879), including names, descriptions, outline-derived profiles, disciplines, topics, methods, prerequisites and planned availability. MCCLITR111 Introduction to Literary Studies, MCCLITR112 Great Literary Works, MCCLITR211 World Myth & Literature, MCCLITR212 Life & Travel Writing, MCCLITR311 Film & Text and MCCLITR312 Perspectives on Literary Meaning provide substantial comparative literary study. MCCCOMM211 Style & Meaning adds linguistic and close-reading methods; HCBCOGN312 Psycholinguistics studies language acquisition, use and comprehension; and the communication, film, media, history, sociology and heritage offerings support analysis of culture, identity, colonialism, decolonial critique and representation. The workbook nevertheless contains no French-language course at any level, no staged speaking, listening, grammar, phonetics or academic-writing sequence in French, no French linguistics, no historical sequence in French literature, no dedicated French or Francophone cultural-studies course, no French-medium research seminar and no French-focused thesis. Psycholinguistics is a general cognitive-science course rather than language instruction, and the literature and media courses are comparative English-medium offerings rather than a French/Francophone disciplinary spine. No academically honest 24-course closest match can therefore supply the target programme's cumulative language proficiency and area-specific formation.

provenance.existing_curriculum_context: The latest complete official programme table accounts for exactly 180 EC: 60 EC per year. Year 1 integrates normal cellular, molecular and organ-system structure and function with a care internship, academic/scientific training, communication and professional skills, ethics, law, prevention, health promotion, technology and the medical progress test. Year 2 advances through disease mechanisms, pharmacology and integrated clinical-problem blocks supported by longitudinal academic and professional formation. Year 3 preserves 15 EC of genuine faculty elective space and combines reproduction, mental health and hormones, ageing and emergency-care problem blocks with clinical skills, early practice contacts, academic critical appraisal and the progress test. The bachelor endpoint is distributed across assessed clinical and research outputs rather than isolated as one separately credited thesis.

provenance.existing_comparator_source_notes: The current Leiden and LUMC programme pages confirm the three-year Medicine bachelor and its continuing structure: first-year cellular, molecular, organ-system, academic and professional foundations with patient contact; second-year disease mechanisms and clinically integrated problem blocks; and third-year faculty choice space, clinically oriented problem blocks, clinical skills and longitudinal academic and professional formation. The latest complete target-specific official table accounts for 60 EC in each year. Year 3 begins with 15 EC of genuine faculty elective space, preserved without inventing a choice. The bachelor endpoint is assessed through the CAT project, internal-medicine and neurological examinations, and the selected half-minor report rather than a separately credited thesis course. The programme has no formal route or specialisation requiring selection.

HCBGATE101 Foundation of Life, Health & Biomedicine, HCBLIFE211 Molecular Cell Biology, HCBLIFE212 Human Physiology, HCBLIFE213 Biochemistry, HCBLIFE214 Life Science Laboratory and HCBLIFE311 Molecular Pathology & Genetics provide substantial biomedical foundations. HCBBIOM211 Functional Anatomy, HCBBIOM311 Pharmacology, HCBBIOM312 Infection & Immunity and HCBBIOM313 Mechanisms of Disease add advanced biomedical content; HCBGATE102 Introduction to Brain & Behavior and the cognition and psychology sequences cover neural, behavioural and mental-health perspectives; HCBBIOM111 Epidemiology & Public Health, HCBPSYC311 Medical & Health Psychology and quantitative research courses add population, behavioural and evidence perspectives. The workbook nevertheless contains no supervised clinical placement or patient-care course, no patient interviewing and physical-examination sequence, no longitudinal clinical-skills assessment, no integrated diagnostic-reasoning curriculum, no medicine-wide progress testing, and no comprehensive clinical-problem progression across organ systems and life stages. The available biomedical courses therefore support a biomedical-science alternative, not the profession-defining academic and clinical formation of Medicine.

cases.existing_substantive_exception_reason: Leiden Classics is defined by cumulative ancient Greek and Latin language acquisition, sustained reading of prose and poetry in both original languages, philological and linguistic analysis, and advanced independent reading and research across the two languages. UCR offers valuable study of ancient history, archaeology, philosophy, literature, myth, art and reception, but no Greek or Latin language-acquisition sequence and no curriculum of primary classical texts in the original languages. Those are not peripheral specialist additions: they organize the Leiden programme from the first year through the thesis. A UCR ancient-world pathway would therefore be a defensible Ancient Studies programme, but not a defensible comparator for this language-and-philology-centred Classics degree.

provenance.existing_curriculum_context: The latest complete official programme table accounts for exactly 180 EC: 60 EC per year. Year 1 contains 20 EC of Greek and Latin language acquisition and 20 EC of original-language prose, rhetoric, drama and lyric/elegy, integrated with ancient history, philosophy, literary theory and literary history. Year 2 continues Greek and Latin texts, epic, drama, Greek linguistics and Renaissance Latin while adding material culture, source transmission, philosophy of science and a restricted ancient-philosophy choice. Year 3 preserves 30 EC of genuine free choice and requires 15 EC of advanced Greek/Latin reading, late-antique philosophy and religion, and a 10-EC thesis; both classical languages must remain represented.
provenance.existing_comparator_academic_year: Current programme checked 2026-10-07; latest complete official curriculum table 2025-2026
provenance.existing_comparator_source_notes: The current official programme page confirms Classics as an integrated study of ancient Greek and Latin language and literature, ancient history, philosophy, archaeology and the later reception of antiquity. The latest complete target-specific official study guide supplies a coherent 180-EC structure: 60 EC in each year. Year 1 combines four 5-EC Greek and Latin acquisition modules with four original-language literature courses and history, philosophy, literary theory and literary history. Year 2 continues original-language prose, drama, epic, linguistics and Renaissance Latin alongside material culture, source transmission, philosophy of science and a restricted thematic choice. Year 3 preserves 30 EC of genuine free-choice space and requires a Greek or Latin workshop, an independent reading list in the other language, late-antique philosophy and religion, and a 10-EC thesis. No formal route or specialization is selected.
provenance.existing_ucr_course_evidence: Reviewed all 151 records in the current GitHub main data/reference/ucr_courses_enriched.xlsx (SHA-256 7bf6c2ae9de0837086ec741c27bd94ed7e85dff2d25bde619ecd50cc4d685879), including names, descriptions, outline-derived profiles, disciplines, topics, methods, prerequisites and planned availability. MCCHEAM112 Introduction to World Archaeology, MCCHEAM213 Greek Archaeology, MCCHEAM315 Heritage & Ancient Democracy, GOSHIST213 Western Way of War, GOSPHIL111 Introduction to Western Philosophy, MCCLITR111 Introduction to Literary Studies, MCCLITR112 Great Literary Works and MCCLITR211 World Myth & Literature provide substantial ancient-world, philosophical, literary and material-culture perspectives; MCCHEAM212 Renaissance Italy & Global Mediterranean and MCCCOMM111 The Art of Rhetorical Communication support reception and rhetoric. The workbook nevertheless contains no ancient Greek course, no Latin course, no cumulative grammar and vocabulary sequence, no sustained original-language reading of Greek and Roman prose and poetry, no classical philology or Greek linguistics sequence, and no advanced Greek/Latin independent reading. Because those missing elements constitute the degree's continuous disciplinary spine, the available ancient-history, archaeology and literature courses support Ancient Studies rather than a defensible Classics match.

cases.existing_substantive_exception_reason: Leiden International Studies is not merely a broad collection of global politics, economics, history and culture courses. Every student selects one world region, studies that region through all four disciplinary perspectives, completes a cumulative 25-EC associated-language sequence plus a 5-EC language-and-culture-in-practice course, and writes an area-specific thesis. UCR offers strong adjacent work in international relations, economics, history, law, sociology, media and sustainability, but its current curriculum contains only one general Dutch course and no sustained regional-language sequence. It also lacks a coherent four-perspective area curriculum for any one of the eight Leiden regions. Filling 24 UCR slots with globally oriented courses would therefore reproduce breadth while discarding the degree's defining language-plus-regional-specialisation architecture.

provenance.existing_curriculum_context: The latest complete official study-guide table accounts for exactly 180 EC: 60 EC per year. Year 1 establishes academic literacy, cultural studies, economics, politics, sociolinguistics and world history, then begins a selected region through culture/language, history and 10 EC of language acquisition. Year 2 adds the region's economy and politics, cross-cultural communication, research methods, global political economy, international relations, philosophy of science, a thematic seminar and 15 further EC in the same language. Year 3 contains 30 EC of genuine elective space and requires a 10-EC consultancy project, 5 EC of language and culture in practice, and a 15-EC area-specific thesis. Africa with Arabic is instantiated only by the official-order tie-break; the same structural mismatch applies to all eight areas and their linked languages.
provenance.existing_comparator_academic_year: Current programme checked 2026-10-07; latest complete official curriculum table 2025-2026
provenance.existing_comparator_source_notes: The current official programme page confirms that students choose one of eight world regions and an associated language, combine cultural, historical, political and economic approaches, and complete research methods, a thematic seminar, 30 EC of elective space, the PRINS consultancy project and an area-specific thesis. The latest complete official study guide supplies a coherent 180-EC structure: 60 EC in each year. Africa and Arabic are selected by the neutral official-order tie-break for the generic target. Genuine elective space remains open, and no host courses or minor are invented.
provenance.existing_ucr_course_evidence: Reviewed all 151 records in the current GitHub main data/reference/ucr_courses_enriched.xlsx (SHA-256 7bf6c2ae9de0837086ec741c27bd94ed7e85dff2d25bde619ecd50cc4d685879), including names, descriptions, outline-derived profiles, disciplines, topics, methods, prerequisites and planned availability. BENECON111 Introduction to Economics, BENECON211 International Macroeconomics, GOSPOLI212 Theory of International Relations, GOSPOLI313 Peace & Conflict, GOSHIST111 Modern History, GOSHIST211 History of Empires, GOSLAWJ111 Human Rights: Law & Philosophy, GOSLAWJ212 Introduction to Public International Law, GOSSOCI212 Qualitative Research Methodology and ENSDELT312 Governance of Sustainability cover much of the global economics, politics, history, justice, methods and sustainability breadth. MCCHEAM211 African Art & Heritage and MCCMEDI311 Media & Race provide valuable regionally relevant cultural perspectives, while BENENTR312 International Business & Governance and the communication curriculum support international professional applications. However, the workbook has no Arabic course and no cumulative foreign-language pathway; MCCCOMM112 Dutch is the only named language-acquisition course. It also has no four-course Africa sequence spanning culture/language, history, economy and politics, and no language-in-practice course or area-specific thesis seminar. Other Leiden routes face the same absence of a linked 30-EC language progression and coherent regional spine. These omissions affect the organizing structure of all three years and cannot be repaired through the 30-EC elective space.
